sources.entry: muCommander - A lightweight, cross-platform file manager with a dual-pane interface.

summary.one_liner: muCommander is a lightweight, cross-platform, dual-pane file manager written for any operating system with Java support.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes muCommander as a lightweight, cross-platform file manager with a dual-pane interface. It states it runs on any operating system with Java support, naming macOS, Windows, Linux, *BSD and Solaris. The README covers contribution workflow (issues, fork-and-pull-request, translations, GitHub Discussions) and developer setup. It explains building and running with the Gradle wrapper, including a debug mode that attaches a debugger on a chosen port. It also documents packaging commands for a macOS DMG, a Windows EXE, and Linux TGZ, RPM and DEB distributions.
use_cases: managing files on macOS, Windows or Linux
running a Java-based file manager on BSD or Solaris
contributing code or translations to an open-source file manager
building installers for macOS, Windows or Linux
how_to_run: Install a JDK 11 or later and Git
From the repository root, run: ./gradlew run
For a clean build, run: ./gradlew clean run
To build a Linux TGZ distribution, run: ./gradlew clean tgz
notable: Dual-pane file manager that runs on any Java-supported OS
Gradle wrapper build with a single run command
Packaging targets for DMG, EXE, TGZ, RPM and DEB
caveats: Requires a Java Development Kit (JDK 11 or later) to build and run
The macOS build is unsigned, so Gatekeeper may report it as damaged; the README gives a quarantine-removal workaround
